Question: How can you get over someone who doesn't care about you, but keeps coming back and breaking your heart all over again?
Answer: Every time they come back around, you remain indifferent, say no and stop allowing them back in. You stop putting your life on hold for them, no longer make yourself easily accessible/available, go no contact and never reach out to them again. This gets very easy and is even a decision that comes naturally to you when you have self-worth and self-respect. Because nobody who truly loves and respects themselves will tolerate dynamics of unrequited love and wont chase after or pursue a relationship with someone emotionally unavailable who doesn’t want them, who, through their actions and behaviors, has consistently revealed that they don’t have their best interest at heart.

To a large degree, modern society still operates from the deeply flawed belief that a man has to build and earn value whereas a woman is born with value and needs to preserve it This is a deeply flawed belief because by default, and if we look at it holistically, all of us are of equal value and our value or worth isn’t even something that can be measured. Because of that, pretty much all of us modern men have no choice but to buy into this belief that we need to build and earn our value. However, a lot of other modern men struggle to accept this and refuse to 'build their value', and this is what keeps them single. It makes them feel like they will never be valued even if they put in the effort. Even when they don’t have the looks, money, self-confidence, success and status yet. That they’re simply still growing, learning, developing themselves and discovering who they are. And that they need to get better at picking the right women for themselves, because a lot of times, men go for women who don’t want them and ignore those who do want them. A bunch of modern women aren’t all that either This is because they don’t really have an incentive to develop their personality and to focus on personal growth. They don’t need to learn how to transcend their own ego because there will always be a needy man with no self-respect out there who will validate her. Question: Do individuals who cheat typically feel guilty after being caught? What are some common signs of guilt in this situation?

Those people are someone who cheated because they never really wanted and don’t respect the one they cheated on or someone who had to escape an abusive relationship with a narcissist somehow. In my book, the latter is the only case where cheating is justifiable. Then there are narcissists and morally bankrupt people who just don’t give a fuck and don’t see anything wrong with cheating (yes, there are people like this out there). These people are too far gone and will not ever stop cheating, because this behavioral pattern has become too deeply ingrained in their subconscious mind, and it gets increasingly more difficult to change this pattern the longer it goes on and the older they get. Question: How can we move on and find peace with a breakup if we don't get what we need from the other person (closure)?
Answer: Realize that seeking, asking or waiting for closure from your ex is really you believing that: However, the truth and reality is that they don’t have and never had the power to heal you. Rather, at some point you forgot that you already have this power but either never learned how to tap into your natural ability to heal yourself or unlearned how to do that through certain unwanted experiences in past relationships. The other thing is that even if your ex showed up in front of your doorstep right now at this moment and gave you the kind of closure you think you so desperately need, it would only satisfy you in the short-term because no amount of closure you get would ever be enough. Because this need for closure arises from an unprocessed emotional attachment to them. From a dependency on them to feel and be a certain way. As long as this attachment controls your reality, your ex will have more control and power over you than they’re supposed to have. And unfortunately, some exes will be so narcissistic and egotistical that they exploit this for ego-boosts. They will use that attachment against you. So, here’s how to transcend this: Practice radical acceptance This means that you completely accept things for what they are and stop denying, judging or fighting against them. Because as long you keep waiting for them to save you, you wont be able to completely heal and get back on track. It means to accept that whatever you two had is now over, hasn’t created the results both of you wanted and that the ending you got isn’t the ending you wanted but the one you need. Because how can you know for sure that the ending you got is entirely bad? How do you know if this won’t lead you to something better because it caused you to shift inward and awaken to your true power? How do you know that this adversity is bad for you? Readjust and realign Life is often times unpredictable and things wont always go according to our plan. Things wont always unfold the way we want them to unfold. This is a universal truth that everyone of us experiences. Nobody is immune to this despite the best planning and best preparations. However, one of the most powerful things you can do here is learn to adapt and adjust to the setbacks and adversities life gives you. To emotionally and psychologically adapt to the changes the breakup has initiated in your life. You do so by controlling what you can control and giving up control over what you can’t control. What you can control is how you proceed from here, what you do, how you think and what kind of decisions you make. You already know where you stand with them It‘s not what you want but this is giving you a solid foundation to work and get started with.

Question: What is the best revenge against your ex who emotionally destroyed you?

So, by remaining very hateful and bitter towards this person, you’re actually giving them more power and just what they want — for you to never heal from the wound they inflicted onto you and for you to stay where they need you to stay, which is powerless, depressed, discouraged, miserable, hopeless, insecure and chasing after them. That’s why going out of your way to hurt them in return isn’t the right thing to do, even though it feels right and even though your desire for revenge is completely justified. The wiser and more powerful approach here is this: Be aware of their karma I’m not talking about the kind of karma that most people think of. I.e. where people get back what they send out. The kind of karma I’m talking about is the fact that your ex is the kind of person who is being punished every minute of the day for as long as they remain as toxic, narcissistic and unhealed as they are. They’re the ones who experience massive anxiety and deep feelings of shame when they go to sleep at night and wake up in the morning. They won’t be able to experience something like genuine inner peace for long because of that. And again, this wont stop until they themselves decide to heal whatever core-wounds cause their dysfunctional behaviors. So this is one of the many others ways your ex is already being punished right now for all the things they did to you. It’s the deep shame and the pain that they carry within themselves. The guilt that haunts them and which they try so hard to avoid, ignore and deny every day. This is a pretty shit way to live. So you can rest assured that even though your ex may present themselves as all happy and doing well outwardly, deep down they know that they’re a loser and consistently struggle with feelings of deep worthlessness. Most exes who emotionally destroyed their bf/gf end up regretting it down the line Because at some point they come to the realization of just how damn broken and toxic their own behavior was and of how the breakup was like 80% on them alone. And therein lies another piece of karma for them — it’s that if they ever arrive at this point where they genuinely want to heal and improve themselves, the only way for them to do so is to transcend their ego and pride, which is a pretty painful and dark process. To accept the truth that they hurt, abused and pushed away someone amazing, someone with whom they could have had a really good relationship with and that they royally fucked things up with you to the point of no return. They will have to live with the truth that they’re never going to be with you again and that they themselves are mostly responsible for this outcome. And all that will happen while they see you slipping away, healing and thriving without them more and more. While they have to watch you being happy with the person who doesn’t go out of their way to destroy you. And while they see how ineffective their attempt to break you was. They will feel this pain very deeply and on every level.

Question: Should I wish my ex a happy birthday?
Answer: A lot of people ask themselves this question. Here’s what you need to know about it: Your intention behind it matters the most Generally speaking, it‘s not inherently wrong to send a quick birthday text. Especially not if you’re on relatively good terms and don’t end every interaction on a really toxic and resentful note. However, a lot of people use their exes birthday as an excuse to: And this is when sending this seemingly innocent text is a mistake. Because if you are hoping for more, that your ex will be so glad you sent that text that they will forget the breakup ever happened and thus take you back, then the intention behind these birthday wishes came from the wrong place. Because when you‘ve done that for one or all 3 of the above mentioned reasons, you‘re lying to yourself, it will backfire and it’s essentially the same as if you directly asked your ex to take you back (which never works). On the other hand, if you really weren't hoping for more and couldn’t care less if they responded or not, then it came from the right place, namely from a place of non-attachment and indifference. However, most people who are at this point don’t send birthday wishes to an ex. So again, before you even send such a text, ask yourself what’s the point and what’s your intention behind it. You got to be honest with yourself about this. You‘re not obligated to send birthday wishes Now I know you may be thinking: 'But we used to be so close together and share a past history. Therefore, isn’t sending such a text/giving such a gesture natural?' Yes and no. Yes because you indeed once shared a life together. No because, well, you broke up and whatever you had is now over and in the past. Therefore, you‘re no longer an integral part of each others lives. Also no because it’s perfectly okay and even the more effective approach to never reach out to them again, especially if you’re not on good terms or if you already set up no contact and healed to the point where you authentically enjoy your new life without them.

Question: Why do most people judge everything you do in society?
Answer: Because judging others feels good. It makes people temporarily forget their own problems, past fuckups, self-destructive behaviors, stupid decisions and character flaws. It gives them a sense of pride that often feels like self-confidence but isn’t true self-confidence. Thus, they constantly watch everything you do, hoping that you will make a mistake so that they can then judge you for it and thus feel like they’re not a loser. Question: How do I deal with someone choosing someone else over me?
Answer: If you love this person, then you also respect them and thus have their best interest at heart, even if that love and the feelings you experience for them are unrequited. So because being with you isn’t in their own best interest (at least for them), you have kind of a spiritual obligation to let them go, to walk towards something better and wish them the best with the person they chose over you. You may not understand why they chose that other person over you but, neither do you need to understand it, because that’s not relevant and you don’t wanna go down the route of comparing yourself to the other person they chose over you, competing for their love/attention/respect/whatever or of falling into this downward spiral of self-doubt and constantly overanalyzing what the hell is wrong with you that may have caused them to reject you. What you need to understand is how to successfully let them go, walk towards something better, wish them well and heal yourself. Here’s how to do that: Go no contact This means no friendship, no occasional meeting up, no constantly checking their social media, none of that sort. Because staying in touch while the unrequited love you experience for them runs deep will slowly eat you up inside and corrode your self-confidence. After all, you’re worthy of being loved the way you love someone else. Don’t allow desperation to make you tolerate a dynamic of unrequited love. Choose to respect yourself instead. Realize that if being with you isn’t in their own best interest, pursuing a relationship with them isn’t in your best interest either. You’ll only be setting yourself up as part of a love triangle, and such dynamics usually get toxic and painful very quickly. Therefore, congratulate them for having met their match but at the same time, say your goodbyes, close the door and leave this chapter behind you. Cutting the ties doesn’t mean this person never meant anything to you It’s an act of self-respect and even necessary to be able to operate from your best and most powerful self. Don’t let people tell you otherwise. Just because they’re used to and settle with low relationships doesn’t mean you have to do the same. There are women/men out there who will be as happy about you choosing them as you would have been if your person picked you over their current boyfriend/girlfriend Nobody knows when you meet those people. As long as you’re not completely closed off to relationships and dating, it can happen tomorrow, 6 months from now or in 10 years. But don’t desperately wait for it to happen. Until it happens, keep doing you. Invest in yourself, make yourself as attractive as you can and build a good life for yourself. More often than not, it will happen and develop organically as you’re living life and put yourself out there.

She wouldn’t have such an insatiable craving for and addiction to male attention that she needs to manipulate multiple men into chasing her so thar she feels worthy and good enough. However, we‘re not living in a perfect world. We‘re living in a time where modern dating is pretty toxic and broken. Where a lot of people out there have deep resentment for the opposite gender and will juggle multiple boyfriends/girlfriends, and often times they do so in secret, behind the scenes. They will have a couple of side-guys/side-chicks to cope with their fear of solitude, their self-hatred or with the fact that their 'main-guy/girl' rejected and doesn’t want them. They need an emotional bandaid to get over this, because they don’t know how to do that on their own and without manipulating others. And because of that, they’re not a keeper. They’re not able to build a relationship that’s solid, healthy, secure and based on mutual respect, love and deep alignment. Not until they heal the core-wounds that cause them to behave this way. Unfortunately, you can’t really help them in that regard, especially not if they don’t respect you, don’t view you as an equal and just don’t want to heal (there a lot of people like that out there). Because of that, you got to protect your inner peace by dumping her and walking away, towards something better. You got to stop tolerating being someones side-person, to stop giving 90% while she’s giving you less than 1%. You got to respect yourself and choose people who choose you as their 'main-guy/girl'. Someone who doesn’t need side-guys/girls in the first place.

Question: Why is my ex so cold after our breakup? It’s as if there was no good time between us. Is it a way to push me far from her?
Answer: Years, months or weeks before an ex physically breaks up with you, they’re going through a process of emotionally and psychologically breaking up with you where they constantly find themselves on the verge between letting go and staying. When you are kind to them, they may choose to stay a little longer as a way to see if the relationship improves and if both of you improve your behaviors. When neither of these two happens, your ex reaches a point where they are fed up, finally make up their mind and choose to walk away for good. Once this point is reached, it’s over and they will be fixated on never being with you again in any way, shape or form. At least for the foreseeable future. Any chasing, pursuing, begging or trying to convince them to stay once they made up their mind will only push them away further as a reconciliation is the last thing they want to do right after having made the difficult decision to leave (yes, breakups are difficult for dumpers too). This is also why they appear so cold towards all your approaches. Through their silence, rejection and avoidance, they just want you to get the hint, to accept that it’s over and move on. Give them space and give them the breakup that they want. In the meantime, focus on rediscovering life without them. Realize that you can no longer expect to get the boyfriend/girlfriend treatment from them and remain consistent with no contact.

Question: How do you keep from texting your ex?
Answer: The mindset and approach that always worked well for me and still works like a charm especially in the beginning of no contact is to visualize how right now at this moment where you want to text them, they’re either on a fun date or being wildly intimate with and fucked by whoever they’re currently dating. Think of how they’re lying next to each other right now. Also think of how when you text them, it may not be your ex that’s writing the response but the girl/guy they’re having sex with and lying next to. Then make a conscious and intentional decision to not be that kind of ex. Decide to be the ex who heals and lets go. The ex who your ex wishes would text or call them while they’re lying next to another person in bed at night. The ex who has accepted that it’s over, wishes them well and rediscovers life without them. Who realizes that the only reason you want to text and get a response from them in the first place is because that’s what would feed and strengthen the unhealthy emotional attachment that keeps you bound to them againsr your will. That, with the power of awareness and letting go, you have the ability and skill to rise above such lower instincts, impulses and knee-jerk reactions.

Question: What do I do when my ex wont respect boundaries? We agreed to stay friends but he keeps overstepping and making me feel uncomfortable. He even refused to initially break up even though he was manipulative. He needs help so what do I do?
Answer: Realize that you cannot possibly change or ‘fix’ him. Countless people have tried this before you and all of them ended up either with emotional traumas or wasting many years of their life in a situationship they know very well they should have just walked away from when they had the chance. You’re not the exception to this. So, stop being so naive and instead learn from other peoples mistakes. Realize that people like him often have no intention of improving themselves and of respecting anyone. That their apologies don’t mean shit and are just a way to further exploit your naivety and kindness. They don’t give a shit about you and only care about what’s in it for them. They want you to do everything for them and to carry them on hands but they refuse to reciprocate that. It’s unlikely that this will ever change. In fact, you staying with him (be it as friends or lovers) enables this pattern and rewards him for abusing you. So, even if it hurts, go no contact on him. Refuse to participate in your own abuse. Choose to respect yourself.

Question: Is it bad to date right after a breakup?
Answer: It’s not optimal, because nobody is immune to the workings of the subconscious mind. Now what I mean by this is that if it was a real relationship and if you genuinely loved this person, the breakup will hurt you just as much as it will hurt anyone else. This applies irrespective of how strong, self-confident, experienced, wise, attractive and powerful you think you are. It will also drastically affect the kind of men and women you attract. Because when you haven’t done any healing work post-breakup whatsoever, you’re not healed and stable enough yet to build a healthy, stable and amazing long-term commitment with someone else. You simply wont be able to attract emotionally healthy men or women but are extraordinarily likely to attract men or women who mirror the level of hurt and unprocessed baggage you still carry. Who are manipulative, narcissistic, toxic, non-committal, etc. Because we attract who we are, not who we want. Unfortunately, so many people today don’t realize this. They overestimate how quickly they can heal from a breakup and let go of an ex and underestimate the work and effort this really takes. As a result of that, they consistently find themselves in broken, short-lived, low quality dead-end relationships and eventually start believing that there’s no love out there or thst all good men and good women are gone. When in reality, they’re just not a match to good men and good women who did the healing work and genuinely let go of their ex. So, that’s why at least in my book, we can’t expect to attract emotionally healthy, loyal and good partners if we don’t embody these things ourselves. It‘s also why prioritizing solitude for a couple of months as a way to work on oneself, rediscover life without the ex and heal is so much better and more effective than jumping from relationship to relationship.

Question: We broke up recently and she is already in a relationship. What does it mean?

Your part that contributed to this may just have been that you became too needy, compliant and weak to the point where she lost respect. Invest in yourself and take enough space and time to process and let go of your feelings so that you heal properly while she’s out there constantly trying to escape herself.

Question: How can I tell if my ex is manipulating me?
Answer: Are they consistently reciprocating? Are they openly and honestly talking about whats going on in their mind and with their feelings? Are they showing you through their behaviors and actions that they are committed to improve and solve your relationship problems as much as you are? Are they saying no to opportunities to date other men/women or some of their exes? Do they respond well to your approaches towards them? If most of these answers are a no for you, then you‘re dealing with a manipulative ex who either just wants to use you as a rebound or for ego gratification and attention. In which case the only wise and rational thing to do here is to set up no contact.

Question: My ex moved on so fast. How can I overcome the pain?
Answer: Simply put, because they have been prepared and you weren't. On their side, there has been a process of emotionally and mentally checking out while you were still together and while you were under the impression that everything is cool. I.e. you thought that you had the perfect deal whereas they had already made up their mind and just weren't as emotionally invested in it as you were. This happened long or shortly before they physically left. And during this process, they either started seeing someone new who they planned to secure as their rebound option or were busy creating their post-breakup plan. This is why you can't expect them to feel anything close to what you're feeling right now, because you and them are on a completely different stage in the healing process. You both are on polar opposites of the scale. This is why comparing yourself to them in terms of the healing process isn't going to help you in any way, shape or form. So, don't try to compete with them. Instead, focus on taking care of, solving and healing what you are experiencing right now. What they do doesn't matter and it's completely irrelevant to your healing process, though it’s valid to hate and judge them harshly for leaving the way they did.

Question: Can you provide an example of rebound behavior?
Answer: When your girlfriend or boyfriend is about to dump you and ready to jump into a rebound relationship, very often they will suddenly pull away and become very avoidant. This is the point where they may have already cheated, where they tell you that they ‘need space’ or ‘work on themselves’ and take forever to respond to your texts, calls and approaches. More often than not, they’re not actually working on themselves. They’re just saying it because they would never openly admit to what they’re really doing when they’re distant, which is meeting up with their reboundee. However, because their reboundee is either still in a relationship themselves or for whatever reason hasn’t made up their mind about your person yet, both of them find themselves in limbo where things aren’t set in stone yet. Because before your person dumps you, they want to make sure that they can immediately jump into a relationship with their reboundee, that their reboundee is fully available. Thus, they go back and forth on each other. The way to approach this effectively is to be the one to initiate the breakup and not put your life on hold for them, especially if you can intuitively sense that something is happening behind your back. Don’t wait until they themselves tell you it’s over. Don’t allow yourself to be their placeholder. Be the one who tells them to fuck off. This way, the breakup won’t be as painful and you can move on a bit faster.

Question: People make me feel worthless. What should I do?

So that they can temporarily feel better about themselves and raise their own self-esteem at the expense of others, by pulling them down. Staying away from and avoiding such people as much as possible has consistently protected and strengthened my inner peace, emotional health and sanity.

Question: How can you cope with your ex being in a new relationship if you're not comfortable with it?
Answer: The important thing to realize here is that you don’t own them. That they have every right to do this. However, just because they have a right to do this doesn’t mean it’s the right thing to do. In fact, more often than not, quickly jumping into bed with someone new and following it up with a rebound relationship is a mistake that backfires in the long term because they’re merely coping and not healing the underlying breakup-wound. Because they overestimate how quickly they can heal, move on and get over an ex and underestimate the work and effort this really takes. Therefore, even if right now you don’t like this and if it’s hurting you, give them the freedom to make their own mistakes. The consequences of those mistakes aren’t your problem anyway. Because you have your own life right now. You can choose to be wiser and smarter than your ex simply by investing in yourself, prioritizing solitude, rediscovering life without them, rebuilding your self-confidence and healing/growing through your pain. When you consistently do this over months and years (a lot can happen in 6 months), you will be a drastically improved, more healed, more attractive, more aware and more powerful version of yourself. While your ex will be stuck in their old ways, likely won’t have grown or changed for the better much and regret not having believed in you back then. They will eventually want a piece of your new life. But they wont get it. At best, you can give them gratitude for having redirected you to a better path by dumping you.

Question: Is it beneficial to seek closure during a breakup or is it better to move on without looking back?
Answer: In the context of breakups, closure is a byproduct of an unprocessed emotional attachment to your ex. It‘s you waiting for them to give you permission to let them go, to accept that whatever you had is over and to start living your life again. Because you still believe that your ex is responsible for how you feel and that they alone have the power to complete, save and heal you. To make all your problems go away. None of this is true of course. It‘s just a belief. A survival mechanism and outdated thought-pattern that you once assigned a certain meaning to that once served to keep you safe and ensure your survival but no longer serves you now because it’s an outdated belief. Right now, you don’t need anyone outside of you to survive. The power to complete, save and heal you is already and has always been in you but never in your ex. That’s why it’s time to give this belief back to whoever gave it to you. To rediscover and maintain your independence, autonomy and emotional fortitude. So, is it beneficial to seek and wait for closure? The answer is that it only benefits and strengthens the emotional attachment to them. That it reinforces this idea and outdated belief I mentioned above. Other than that, you absolutely don’t need closure. What you need is to learn radical acceptance. To radically accept that:

Question: What are signs of immaturity in personality (psychology)?
Answer: The biggest one is a serious lack of accountability Where someone consistently defaults to playing the victim when the consequences of their actions, behaviors and decisions catch up to them. Where everything is always someone or something elses fault but never their own way of thinking and behaving that co-created the unwanted consequences and circumstances they find themselves in. It‘s pathetic, and people who do this know that. But, they continue to stay in camp victimhood anyway because they’re lacking the maturity to introspect and to own up to their actions, decisions and behaviors. I.e. they usually don’t achieve their goals, consistently fuck their relationships up, throw loved ones under the bus to escape accountability, etc. That’s why we can’t really win in life without a certain degree of personal accountability. Because the level of our success in any area or aspect of our life is proportional to the amount of responsibility we are willing and able to take on.

Question: Why are some people (especially men) so rude to people they don't find attractive?

They feel that being around people they don’t feel attracted to will somehow lower their status in their friends eyes (friends who are most likely just as prideful and egocentric as them). Because of this, rather than showing some basic respect, they choose to let the 'unattractive' person know that they don’t have a chance and must stay away by being unnecessarily rude and inconsiderate of their feelings and value as a human being. Truly kind and decent people do it differently. They don’t assess someones value solely based on surface-level appearances or on how they feel about them. Because they have the growth, wisdom and maturity to look beyond the surface, they can think beyond themselves and let the other know that they’re not attracted to them in a kind and respectful way rather than treating them like a sub-species.

Question: What are some signs that it's time to stop trying to get your ex back?
Answer: Generally speaking, trying to get an ex back is almost never a good approach for a multitude of reasons. Most of all because a lot of people who do want their ex back try to create this result for all the wrong reasons, because they’re operating from a place of fear and neediness, and decisions made from this place are always the wrong decisions. However, for those who tried it anyway, there’s just one sign to look out for, namely: You‘ve been trying all you can for 6 months or more but it either just doesn’t give you any desired results, you’re still stuck in the friendzone or your ex just won’t budge and keeps giving you massive resistance. When this happens, this is the universe giving you an incredibly strong sign that this is not the right person for you anymore, that you have to emotionally let them go, accept that it’s over and walk towards something better. So, don’t listen to people who tell you to 'try harder' and to 'fight for them', for they don’t know what they’re talking about, even if their intentions are to help you. Trying harder beyond the point I mentioned will only make things worse. It may give you a restraining order or more of what you‘ve already gotten — rejection, abandonment and corroded self-confidence. Therefore, you just got to take the loss, respect their decision to leave, move on and decide to heal and rediscover your core-confidence without them. Anything else is insanity, won‘t work and no longer has anything to do with love but everything with low self-esteem, unhealthy codependency and deep attachment problems.
